entries.note: CME first seen to the ESE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-10-17T02:48Z. It is also seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C3. The CME is also seen later in its propagation to the E GOES CCOR-1 near the edge of the  FOV as the early frames of the CME are obscured by Earthshine. It is also seen to the SE in STEREO A COR2 as a partial halo. The leading edge of the CME is somewhat irregularly shared with the nose farther to the south. The source is a filament eruption on or slightly beyond the SE limb best seen in SDO AIA 304 beginning around 2026-10-17T01:00Z. A wide opening of field lines can also been seen in SDO AIA 171 and SDO AIA 193.

Narrow very minor CME/outflow visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The start of the CME/outflow is likely much earlier. No source is found for this CME in EUV imagery.

Faint and narrow CME seen to the E in early SOHO LASCO C2 imagery and not seen in C3, GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery, likely because of its faintness. The start time is likely at least an hour earlier but the CME becomes clear around 17Z. No clear source found, so the CME is likely far sided.

Bright CME seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the NW in STEREO A COR2. Its source is likely a messy eruption seen in the NW quadrant in STEREO A EUV 195/304 and centered very approximately around N12W140 near former Active Region 14549 starting 2026-10-16T14:25Z. Coronal signatures include dimming, post-eruptive arcades and ejecta seen in STEREO A EUV 195/304, as well as opening/moving of field lines behind the NW limb in SDO AIA 193/171.

CME visible faintly to the NE in STEREO A COR2. The CME is not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The potential source is an eruption starting around 2026-10-16T11:00Z, primarily centered around N05E10, although the eruption extends as far east as N05E30. The eruption may include a filament liftoff as seen in SDO AIA 304. Dimming, moving/opening field lines, and post-eruptive arcades are best seen in SDO AIA 193. The eruption is also seen near the NE limb from the point of view of STEREO A EUV 195 and 304 imagery. This CME may exhibit deflection due to its proximity to the coronal hole.

CME visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely beyond the east limb, as moving/opening field lines are seen in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA as early as 2026-10-16T10:28Z.

CME faintly visible to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2. The source for this CME is not found in available EUV imagery, and the CME may be farsided.
Narrow CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. No source is found for this CME in EUV imagery.

Faint, wide CME visible to the SW in STEREO A COR2 only. The CME is not clearly seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The potential source is not clearly visible. There is a data gap in STEREO A COR2 and EUV imagery in real-time from 2026-10-15T12:09Z to 2026-10-16T06:09Z. A potential source may be seen in STEREO A EUV imagery anywhere from longitudes W90 to approximately W120 as a gradual, minor dimming may be seen after the data gap starting around 2026-10-16T06:09Z. However, there are not strong post-eruption signatures in imagery, and there is low confidence in this analysis of the source location.

CME seen to the ESE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source may be some minor field line movement beyond the ESE limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning as early as 2026-10-15T18:00Z.

CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-10-14T23:12Z. The source of this event is a large filament eruption seen originating from beyond the NE limb in GOES SUVI 304 imagery beginning at approx. 2026-10-14T21:52Z. Field line opening is also seen in GOES SUVI 284 in association with this eruption.

CME seen to the West in STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-10-14T22:09Z following the end of a data gap. This CME is not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 as it is likely obscured by the occulting disk. The source of this CME may be related to an unstable filament seen along the West limb in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery beginning at approx. 2026-10-14T18:45Z.

Bright CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-10-14T13:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a filament eruption centered at approx. N45E20 seen beginning at approx. 2026-10-14T10:05Z in SDO AIA, GOES SUVI and STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery. Dimming and field line opening can also be seen in SDO AIA 171/193, GOES SUVI 284 and STEREO A EUVI 195 imagery.

Narrow CME first seen to the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-10-12T19:36Z, as well as by GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which began at 2026-10-12T18:58Z. The source of this event is rising field line loops seen originating from beyond the SW limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning at approx. 2026-10-12T18:18Z.

This CME is visible to the west in STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is likely related to a filament eruption visible beyond the western limb in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery which lifts-off around 2026-10-12T10:15Z.
This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures visible on the Earth or STEREO A-facing disk.

This CME is visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a filament eruption spanning S12E15 to S20E30 which begins to lift off around 2026-10-12T04:45Z as seen in SDO 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. Dimming is visible in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 195 imagery, with post eruptive arcades visible starting around 2026-10-12T05:45Z.

This CME is visible to the southwest in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. This event is not seen in STEREO A COR2 in real-time due to a data gap starting at 2026-10-11T17:38Z. The source may be related to dimming centered near S20E30 starting around 2026-10-11T22:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 195 imagery.

This CME is visible to the east in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. This event is seen in STEREO A COR2, directed towards the east, after it has exceeded the field of view due to a data gap from 2026-10-11T17:38Z to 2026-10-12T01:53Z. The source is a filament eruption spanning S30E30 to S10E05 which begins to lift off around 2026-10-11T22:30Z as seen in SDO 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery. Dimming is visible in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 195 imagery, with post eruptive arcades visible starting around 2026-10-11T23:40Z.

Outflow first seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-10-11T09:12Z. This feature is much easier to see later in its propagation into SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is most likely outflow following CME: 2026-10-10T16:15Z but may be related to field line movement seen near the NW limb in SDO AIA 193 starting as early as 2026-10-11T05:00Z.
Minor faint, narrow CME/outflow seen to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and covered by the data gap in STEREO A. No clear source has been found for this CME.
